requirements.title: A multiple subscript expands to a sequence of consecutive dimension subscripts
requirements.definition: A multiple-subscript specifies a sequence of subscripts whose length is the size of the multiple-subscript expression. The effect is as though the individual values in that sequence appeared as ordinary subscripts for consecutive dimensions, without the @ marker. The rank-one, integer-expression, and section-subscript grammar restrictions are owned by 9.5.3.1.

pending.sequence-length-equals-multiple-subscrip: PENDING positive-control source shape: rank-three INTEGER array with distinct coordinate-coded literals and INTEGER v(2)=[2,1], use a(@v,2) or a(1,@v). Independent oracle is the literal selected by exactly two values from v plus the remaining scalar subscript. Non-vacuous because using only one value from v or three dimensions selects a different literal or rank.
pending.values-fill-consecutive-dimensions: PENDING positive-control source shape: rank-four array with literals encoding (i,j,k,l), use a(9,@[2,3],4) and check the literal for coordinates (9,2,3,4). Non-vacuous because reversing the vector or assigning it to nonconsecutive dimensions changes the literal.
pending.at-marker-not-retained-after-expansion: PENDING source-classification contrast: compare a(@[1,2]) with ordinary a(1,2) as scalar element designators using the same literal oracle. Non-vacuous because the same source also includes a([1,2],1) as a vector-subscript section dependency, showing the @ form is not retained as a vector subscript. Any invalid contrast is attributable to 9.5.3.1 rank/classification owners, not this effect rule.

requirements.title: Omitted multiple subscript triplet expressions use lower bounds, upper bounds, and stride one
requirements.definition: In a multiple-subscript-triplet, an omitted first int-expr has the effect of a rank-one array whose element values are the lower bounds of the corresponding dimensions, an omitted second int-expr has the effect of a rank-one array whose element values are the upper bounds of the corresponding dimensions, and an omitted third int-expr has the effect of appearing with value one.

pending.omitted-first-uses-corresponding-lower-b: PENDING positive-control source shape: rank-two explicit-shape array with nondefault lower bounds, use a(@:[u1,u2]) where the upper vector is literal and lower bounds are declared constants. Independent oracle is SHAPE/SUM from selected lower-bound-starting coordinates. Non-vacuous because explicit first vector [different literals] selects a different SUM.
pending.omitted-second-uses-corresponding-upper-: PENDING positive-control source shape: rank-two array with known upper bounds, use a(@[l1,l2]:) on a non-assumed-size object. Oracle is SHAPE/SUM computed from declared upper bounds. Non-vacuous because adding a smaller explicit second vector changes both shape and SUM; C931 is avoided by not using an assumed-size final multiple triplet.
pending.omitted-third-uses-stride-one: PENDING positive-control source shape: rank-two array with coordinate-coded literals, use a(@[1,1]:[3,3]) and expect all coordinates with unit stride. Non-vacuous because an explicit third vector [2,2] would produce a smaller shape and different SUM.

requirements.title: A multiple subscript triplet expands to conforming subscript triplets with scalar broadcast
requirements.definition: A multiple-subscript-triplet specifies a sequence of subscript triplets whose count is the size of one of its array int-exprs. Any scalar int-expr acts as though broadcast to the shape of an array int-expr. Corresponding elements of the first, second, and third effective arrays act respectively as the first subscript, second subscript, and stride of each generated subscript triplet.

pending.triplet-count-from-array-expression-size: PENDING positive-control source shape: rank-two array with two-element endpoint vectors in one multiple-subscript-triplet, expect a section whose rank/shape reflects two generated triplets. Independent oracle is SHAPE plus SUM from coordinate-coded literals. Non-vacuous because a one-element vector repair changes rank/shape.
pending.scalar-int-expr-broadcast: PENDING positive-control source shape: use @1:[2,3]:1 or @[1,1]:3 on a rank-two array so one scalar endpoint or stride is broadcast across a two-element vector. Oracle is the finite coordinate set from the broadcast value. Non-vacuous because replacing the scalar with a distinct vector changes selected elements.
pending.corresponding-elements-map-to-first-seco: PENDING positive-control source shape: use distinct first, second, and stride vectors, for example @[1,2]:[5,4]:[2,1], and compute the selected coordinates independently. Non-vacuous because swapping the second and third effective arrays would change shape or values.
pending.generated-triplets-feed-section-semantic: PENDING cross-owner positive-control source shape: generated triplets include one empty sequence and one nonempty sequence; oracle is overall size zero from 9.5.3.4.1/9.5.3.4.2. Non-vacuous because changing the empty generated triplet to nonempty yields a literal SUM.
